@notionhq/notion-mcp-server.notes: Notion uses workspace-scoped tokens — surface a workspace picker before the OAuth handshake. The integration must be added to individual pages/databases by the user after authorization. Internal integrations use a plain API key instead of OAuth.

linear-mcp.notes: Linear also supports personal API keys (Settings → API). Prefer API keys for single-user setups; OAuth for multi-user. Access tokens expire after 10 years but can be revoked in the Linear dashboard.

@modelcontextprotocol/server-slack.notes: Slack issues two token types: xoxb- (bot tokens) and xoxp- (user tokens). Use xoxb- tokens for bot actions like posting messages. Use xoxp- tokens only when you need to act as a specific user. The Bot Token Scopes and User Token Scopes are configured separately in the app manifest. Store xoxb- in SLACK_BOT_TOKEN.

@modelcontextprotocol/server-github.notes: GitHub supports both classic PATs and fine-grained PATs. Fine-grained PATs (github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens) are preferred as they are scoped to specific repos and permissions. For OAuth apps the classic scopes still apply. Never use `repo` scope with write access unless the workflow requires commits or PR creation.

@modelcontextprotocol/server-google-driv.notes: Requires access_type=offline in the authorization URL to receive a refresh_token on first auth. Without offline access the token expires in 1 hour with no way to refresh. For domain-wide access in Google Workspace use a Service Account with domain-wide delegation instead of user OAuth.

gmail-mcp.notes: Use access_type=offline and prompt=consent when requesting authorization to guarantee receiving a refresh_token even if the user has previously authorized the app. Use the narrowest scope required: gmail.readonly if write access is not needed. The gmail.modify scope covers labeling and archiving without send permission.

google-calendar-mcp.notes: Requires access_type=offline for refresh tokens. The calendar.events scope allows creating and editing events but not deleting calendars. Use calendar.readonly for read-only access. Google Calendar API has a per-user quota of 1,000,000 queries/day; batch requests if reading many events.
